original_card.question: Can a specified pair of consecutive calls eliminate a restoration that the next call reconstructs?
methods: Write typed entry/exit contracts and a contracting multitype recurrence.
Derive a lower bound for the compulsory transitions of one proposed typed interface.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show actual eliminated work and legal composition; changing a scalar recurrence into a matrix is insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Find a concrete consecutive-call boundary in the selected review and list its entry/exit obligations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Specify two call types and one operation actually removed by composition; derive the normalized recurrence.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Eliminating compulsory boundary work can lower recursive cost beyond packing gains.
allowed_variations: A two-type pilot or one explicit deferred restoration.
scope_change_triggers: Rewriting the old scalar recurrence as a matrix without eliminating work.

actual_scope: All-tree source-restoring additive port borrowing: four-way echoes with three dirty rows; compare the strongest source-protected template recurrence at the same cap.
scope_change_reason: The persistent-boundary card is specialized to changing external source ownership inside descendants, rather than carrying a frame across a selected pair. This admits a higher-arity template at fixed space and removes repeated child work; it is a scoped recursive-interface side result, not a selected-supplier mechanism.
bottleneck_link: A weaker source boundary admits cheaper recursive trees at fixed dirty-array count. The inherited direct all-role moment remains noncontracting, so supplier benefit is unestablished.
stop_rule: One deterministic template experiment; orient within 12 minutes, finish implementation before final verification reserve. Stop if complete modular/access invoice loses its same-cap advantage; do not mine a new kappa.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json, verify.py, oracle.py and PROOF.md; bounded formal-word identities plus written all-tree induction.
author: Hanson Sun (@bbMisk), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, both implementations, verification and prose. No subagents or independent human review.

open_questions.question: Does an actual selected-supplier call permit its source to be borrowed between descendant boundaries?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Without this ownership permission the construction is inadmissible, and no kappa conclusion follows.
open_questions.first_step: Name one concrete call, list every source observer and alias, and check its source contract against the emitted write cuts.
open_questions.blocked_by: No compatible selected-supplier source interval or physical owner map has been identified.
